title: Mercy lets the child tell the truth
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 51
summary: The shabad opens in tenderness and dependence: the soul leans on the Lord's mercy and admits its mistakes as a child would. It then confesses how hard Hukam is to accept and ends in recognition of the Supreme Lord through the Guru.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels stuck between shame and self-protection after failure. Stayed with sincerely, it makes confession safer and trust more childlike.
takeaway: Hold onto this: bring the truth about failure into the Lord's mercy.

lines.translation: Siree Raag, Fifth Mehla, Seventh House:

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੇਰੈ ਭਰੋਸੈ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਮੈ ਲਾਡ ਲਡਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: terai bharosai piaare mai laadd laddaiaa ||
lines.translation: Relying on Your Mercy, Dear Lord, I have cherished and loved you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੂਲਹਿ ਚੂਕਹਿ ਬਾਰਿਕ ਤੂੰ ਹਰਿ ਪਿਤਾ ਮਾਇਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: bhooleh chookeh baarik too(n) har pitaa maiaa ||1||
lines.translation: Like a foolish child, I have made mistakes. O Lord, You are my Father and Mother. ||1||
It is easy to speak and talk,
but it is difficult to accept Your Will. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉ ਮਾਣੁ ਤਾਣੁ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰਾ ਹਉ ਜਾਨਉ ਆਪਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: hau maan taan karau teraa hau jaanau aapaa ||
lines.translation: I stand tall; You are my Strength. I know that You are mine.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭ ਹੀ ਮਧਿ ਸਭਹਿ ਤੇ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਬੇਮੁਹਤਾਜ ਬਾਪਾ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: sabh hee madh sabheh te baahar bemuhataaj baapaa ||2||
lines.translation: Inside of all, and outside of all, You are our Self-sufficient Father. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਿਤਾ ਹਉ ਜਾਨਉ ਨਾਹੀ ਤੇਰੀ ਕਵਨ ਜੁਗਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: pitaa hau jaanau naahee teree kavan jugataa ||
lines.translation: O Father, I do not know-how can I know Your Way?

lines.gurmukhi: ਬੰਧਨ ਮੁਕਤੁ ਸੰਤਹੁ ਮੇਰੀ ਰਾਖੈ ਮਮਤਾ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: ba(n)dhan mukat sa(n)tahu meree raakhai mamataa ||3||
lines.translation: He frees us from bondage, O Saints, and saves us from possessiveness. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਏ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਰਹਿਓ ਆਵਣ ਜਾਣਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhe kirapaal Thaakur rahio aavan jaanaa ||
lines.translation: Becoming Merciful, my Lord and Master has ended my comings and goings in reincarnation.
Meeting with the Guru, Nanak has recognized the Supreme Lord God. ||4||27||97||

structure: First, it begins by linking love to mercy and honest childlike admission.
Then, it admits how easy speech is and how difficult it is to actually accept Hukam.
Finally, it ends with possessiveness loosening and the Supreme Lord being recognized through the Guru.
